thread_analysis.thread_summary: IDEAL company registration completion thread. Customer's product used a Nordic S132-based module. Estimate request specified S132 Subset IDs. After QPRDv3 (July 1, 2024), Subset IDs from the old system cannot be referenced in new registrations — parent QDIDs must be used instead. Allion registered using S140 parent QDIDs (which encompass the S132 subset), and the SIG portal displayed 'S140 xxxx' as the Included Design. Customer noticed the discrepancy and asked for clarification. Allion explained the QPRDv3 Subset ID restriction. Compliance Folder documents were then collected (operation manual, block diagram, outline drawing — Japanese language acceptable) and CD-R was delivered. Thread also includes SIG payment procedural advice: Invoice must be obtained by the registering company's account holder, but the actual wire transfer can be done by a third party (e.g., a parent company).
all_questions_found: Why does the SIG portal show S140 as the Included Design when the product uses S132?
Can Subset IDs from the old qualification system be referenced in QPRDv3 new registrations?
Can Compliance Folder documents be submitted in Japanese?
Can a third party (different company) make the SIG registration fee wire transfer on behalf of the registering company?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: QPRDv3 prohibits new registrations from referencing old-system Subset IDs. The parent QDID must be used, which results in the SIG portal showing the parent QDID name even if the product only implements a subset. This is a common post-QPRDv3 source of customer confusion. For payment: Invoice must be generated by the registering company's SIG account holder; the actual bank transfer can be executed by a different company (parent, affiliate, payment processor), and the Qualification Number will still be assigned to the account that generated the Invoice.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: QPRDv3 Subset ID rule: old Subset IDs → cannot reference directly → must use parent QDID. Compliance Folder documents do not need to be in English — Japanese is acceptable. Invoice ownership determines who receives the Qualification Number, not who makes the payment.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting to reference a Subset ID in a QPRDv3 registration would cause registration failure. Not explaining the S140 substitution to the customer during Review Page confirmation caused confusion — should be proactively communicated.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Allion acknowledged failing to explain the S132-to-S140 parent QDID substitution at the Review Page confirmation stage. This led to a post-submission customer inquiry. The correction should be disclosed and explained before or during the Review Page step.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When substituting parent QDIDs for customer-specified Subset IDs under QPRDv3 rules, explicitly explain the substitution at the Review Page confirmation step. Do not wait for the customer to notice the mismatch after submission.
